comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Root-caused the six-change stack Verified -1 (epic f79d, mirror remediation).

Finding 1 — the -1 votes are against STALE patchsets. Every pushed Gerrit revision differs from every local commit (gerrit 2530=11e669180ba1 2531=908d4f74d3dd 2533=436a687c102e 2535=ca5d08e6fa06 2536=bb76a00a8f55 2537=b7ed793101ab vs local 5a2819b14541 93fa6d1879b1 59b9f9fe8f74 c30c53992be6 f822f4ecb923 936178dad405). The stack was rebuilt locally and never pushed, so CI has never voted on the current code.

Finding 2 — none of the failures was a test failure. Run 33688717373 (change 2537) failed the Public-types drift gate on all four platforms: that gate runs python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types and diffs src/rebar/types.py, a GENERATED file whose header says DO NOT EDIT BY HAND, and F3/F6/F7 all added constants to it. Runs 33687891644 and 33702178549 failed even earlier, in the Gerrit checkout step — git fetch origin misses the change ref on the GitHub mirror and the Gerrit fallback returned HTTP 504 after 60s, the disk-pressured host, i.e. the environmental class. Neither run contains a single FAILED tests/ line.

Finding 3 — at the current local tip gen_types produces no diff; the generator now emits both TICKET_TYPES and PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES, so the drift cause is addressed locally. Whether each INTERMEDIATE commit also passes is unproven and is what the next push will establish.

Method note, recorded because it nearly became a false root cause. I first checked the drift gate per-commit in a detached worktree using PYTHONPATH rather than a real editable install. It reported drift at every commit including the tip, contradicting the clean regeneration in the real worktree. The regenerated file had dropped ALL the enum Literals, meaning the generator could not resolve the schemas — an environment artifact, not evidence. Discarded rather than reported. A per-commit drift check needs a real install per commit.

Also this session: F8 (91b0) implemented and pushed as change 2548, now LLM-Review +1. F9 re-review PASS+signed after its unsatisfiable AC1b was corrected; change 2547 LLM-Review +1. bc66 plan corrected after a justified BLOCK (nothing imports Finding from _cli._registry; the real consumer surface is eight names across 22 files), re-review in flight. F10 plan written with its three drift claims re-verified, file_impact recorded BEFORE review, review in flight. F14 review in flight.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Six-change stack LANDED on origin/main, plus F9.

Merged in original order: d6a1446eea03 Partition ticket types (F3), 5a6f76b126b6 MCP model registry (F5), 3448f22493d1 reducer status vocabulary (F6), eed080bfaf05 cycle-capable relations (F4), 03648d47d4c8 create ticket-type vocabulary (F7), 9cae469af953 op-cert kind vocabulary (F2). Change 2547 (F9, source-kind vocabulary from LAYER_ORDER) merged as a3e4939062d6.

I verified the gates myself before submitting rather than taking the subagent report at face value: all six at LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submittable true, 0 unresolved. Submitted the top of the stack, which submitted its ancestors; all six now MERGED and present on origin/main.

Root cause of the long Verified -1, confirmed independently by two paths. NEITHER hypothesis in the original brief was right, and no CI run in this stack ever contained a single FAILED tests/ line.
(a) src/rebar/types.py is a GENERATED file ("DO NOT EDIT BY HAND", produced by python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types). F3 hand-added PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES/PLAN_REVIEW_REVIEWED_TYPES and F7 hand-added TICKET_TYPES; CI regenerates and diffs, the hand-added block vanishes, every commit in the stack fails the public-types drift gate. Fixed by adding a declaration seam to the generator (_DERIVED_VOCABULARIES keyed by the common.schema.json def each block derives from), so the constants stay in rebar.types as a stdlib-only leaf AND survive regeneration.
(b) The earlier failures were environmental: the Gerrit checkout step got HTTP 504 for 60s during a sustained availability fault that also hit unrelated changes 2541/2542/2545. No fix warranted; new patchsets re-triggered CI.

Two caveats recorded rather than buried. The subagent hit a near-miss during the rebase — a git commit --amend while stopped on a CONFLICT rather than an edit stop folded 2536 into 2535 and collapsed the stack to five; it aborted and redid the rebase correctly, and the final six commits kept their original Change-Ids with no duplicate changes. And it killed a full tests/unit run still going after 23 minutes on this contended box, so no full local suite was personally observed green — CI Verified +1 on every patchset is the authoritative run covering that.

comments.body:
bc66 LANDED — 173b2a6357cf on gerrit/main. F11 (elfin-decagonal-polarbear) is now unblocked: _registry.py is 685 lines on main with _registry_checks.py (170) beside it, so there is headroom for the Route flag F11 must add.

Submitted three green changes this tick, each verified at LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 with submittable=true before submitting: 2550 bc66 (173b2a6357cf), 2548 F8 (b22543d8d30b), 2553 F14 (eac740902160). All three MERGED.

Note for anyone checking: these are visible on gerrit/main but NOT yet on origin/main. origin is the GitHub MIRROR and replication lags the Gerrit merge by minutes — a git log origin/main immediately after a submit will not show the commit, which is mirror lag rather than a failed submit. Confirm against the gerrit remote, or wait for replication.

I deliberately did NOT submit 2549, 2551 or 2552. They are owned by the same RebarBotNava identity but authored by other sessions (2549/2551 are the disk-pressure work another session owns), so owner:self returns them without them being mine to land.

Still open in this epic: 2555 (F10) awaiting Verified; F11 to plan, review and implement; then the seven merged children plus these three to verify and close.
